summary.headline: Finkurve crossed INR 1,096 crore AUM (up 149% YoY) with gross NPA at a record-low 0.13% and CRAR at 30.96% in Q4 FY26.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 AUM of INR 1,096 crore, up 149% YoY from INR 439 crore, with branches rising from 73 to 105. Quarterly total income grew 71% YoY to INR 69 crore and PAT grew 105%, per the CFO. Asset quality was described as a record low, with gross NPA at 0.13% and net NPA at 0.09%. Management also cited a rating upgrade to BBB+ (March 2026, from CARE and Infomerics), a co-lending start with Godrej (about INR 21 crore off-book AUM), and transition to a middle-layer NBFC. Guidance for FY27 is 40-50% AUM growth and about 50% branch expansion, with a cost-of-borrowing assumption of roughly 11.2%.

from INR 237 crore a year earlier per analyst question

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Core franchise; management aims for gold loans to remain the majority of AUM through FY29. Average portfolio LTV about 72% at year-end, and 99% of the book is Stage 1 (under 30 DPD).

segments.name: Personal loans
segments.commentary: About 3.9% of AUM but about 30% of revenue, run in partnership with fintech partners; planned to stay at no more than 10% of AUM.

segments.name: Co-lending
segments.commentary: Started mid-Q4 under CLM-1 with three partners (RBL, Godrej, and one more); off-book AUM about INR 21 crore, under 2% of AUM. Aspiration is 20% of AUM by end-FY27.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 40-50% YoY for FY27; management says it aspires to grow faster but will keep growth risk-adjusted.
Branch expansion of about 50% in FY27 (roughly 150-160 branches from 105); 30-45 days per branch opening, with manpower as the main constraint.
Cost of borrowing assumed at about 11.2% for FY27, the same as FY26; management expects the rating benefit to be already priced in.
Long-term targets over 3-5 years: ROE 17-18% and ROA 3.5-4%; AUM aspiration of about INR 5,000 crore by FY29.
Target debt-to-equity of 4x-4.5x (about 4x on a steady-state basis), excluding off-book co-lending; no equity raise planned in FY27, with a possible review after H1.
capex_capacity: Branch capex about INR 14-15 lakh per branch and opex about INR 2.5-3 lakh per branch per year.
Branch opening takes about 30-45 days; manpower availability is the main constraint rather than technology or infrastructure.
Branch-level technology upgrade for customer onboarding is in progress; management expects the bigger gains in FY27, after AI and automation cut head-office TAT.
Capital headroom: CRAR at about 31% against a 15% regulatory requirement for gold loan NBFCs.
demand_pricing: Management says South India holds most of the INR 19 lakh crore organised gold loan market; Finkurve will stay in South India until its catchment areas saturate, then look at Odisha, Goa or Maharashtra.
Agri lending: standalone NBFC agri PSL books have limited P&L benefit now; agri product to be launched only through a bank co-lending arrangement, timing not set.
Augmont ecosystem cited for lower cost of funds through bank relationships; management said Augmont digital gold customers have not yet been used to source gold loans.
Industry cost of funds expected to rise, but management expects Finkurve to hold or reduce its cost through PSU and private bank mix and co-lending.

qa_highlights.question: Is the co-lending share (under 2% of AUM) on track, and what are the FY27 and FY28 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Co-lending went live only in the last quarter under CLM-1; management aspires to 20% of AUM by end-FY27, with no partner-specific numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-of-borrowing outlook and what does a rating upgrade mean for it?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 average cost of borrowing was 11.2%; FY27 is assumed at about the same. Moving from BBB+ to A- is a multi-factor journey, not expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR 102 crore of cash held, and is it a drag on ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash held as a buffer for April, a seasonally slack month for bank borrowings; management said the balance will be deployed into the loan book.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a profit guidance and a FY29 target?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific profit guidance; AUM aspiration is more than INR 5,000 crore by FY29, with 17-18% ROE and 3.5-4% ROA as five-year benchmarks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the equity raise plan and the leverage target?
qa_highlights.answer: No equity raise planned in FY27 given CRAR at about 31%; debt-to-equity comfort range 4x-4.5x, with about 4x the ideal.

qa_highlights.question: Gold price stress: what is the LTV and what happens if gold falls 15-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Average LTV about 72%; management says it stress-tests at 10-15% falls and reported no portfolio stress when gold fell about 15% in a single day last quarter.

risks_watch: Fee and commission expense is a large cost line (about INR 70 crore finance cost referenced by analyst); fee income fell sharply due to regrouping under Ind AS, so the reported trend is hard to read.
Net worth about INR 346 crore against a 5,000 crore AUM aspiration; the path to capital needs an equity raise or leverage at about 4x debt-to-equity.
Cost of funds is expected to rise industry-wide; management assumes flat 11.2% cost of borrowing despite rating upgrade.
Branch productivity and manpower availability are needed to hit the 150-160 branch target.
Overdue but not NPA figures were not provided on the call; management will follow up by email.
Co-lending target of 20% of AUM by end-FY27 requires a sharp ramp from under 2% today.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, capital and growth, with specific numbers. Cautious on rating-driven cost-of-funds gains, ROE/ROA timing, and profit guidance, which were deferred to multi-year horizons. Evasive on the overdue-not-NPA pipeline and on the Augmont customer sourcing.
key_quotes: Our Q4 numbers have been one of the best-performing quarters wherein our AUM on a YoY basis has grown by 149% from INR 439 crore to INR 1,096 crore.
We aspire to achieve a 20% of the overall portfolio in co-lending by the end of the financial year.
We should not and we cannot expect this immediately in this financial year, but if we achieve more than what we envisage in this financial year, probably at that point in time we can expect.
